Week 7 Appendix: The Week Everything Moved at Once

Nearly thirty protections weakened, a handful strengthened, and the clock barely moved because the currents canceled each other out.

This week (March 1-7, 2025) marked an extraordinarily dense burst of executive action that simultaneously targeted academic institutions, the judiciary, independent agencies, immigration enforcement, and international alliances. The administration issued dozens of executive orders in a single week, ranging from a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve benefiting Trump-aligned crypto interests to dismantling DHS civil rights oversight offices and voice of America. Judicial independence came under direct assault through calls to impeach judges (Boasberg, Englemayer), while the administration simultaneously defied court orders on funding freezes and worker reinstatement. Universities capitulated to funding threats over pro-Palestinian protests, ICE conducted high-profile detentions of green-card holders and students for political speech (Khalil, Chung), and mass federal workforce cuts proceeded across HHS, USDA, VA, and the Department of Education. The week also featured a dramatic reversal of Ukraine policy—pausing military aid and intelligence sharing—alongside a hostile Oval Office confrontation with Zelenskyy, signaling a geopolitical realignment toward Russia.
